provenance.method: Read-only snapshot of existing saved experiments; no new PSCAD runs.

scenario.name: No-fault baseline
scenario.description: Healthy steady state: all five normally-closed radial lines (G01-N02, N02-N03, N03-N04, N03-N05, N05-N06) stay closed and both tie lines (N02-N05, N04-N06) stay open. No controller commands are issued. Use this run to capture reference voltage/current traces for comparison against the fault scenarios.

scenario.name: Single fault isolation
scenario.description: A fault at N03 trips its three incident breakers (SW_N02_N03, SW_N03_N04, SW_N03_N05). Both tie lines stay open, so N04, N05 and N06 are left de-energized -- no restoration path is taken. Use this to characterize the isolation transient and the resulting de-energized island, before comparing against the tie-switch-restoration scenario.

scenario.name: Tie-switch restoration
scenario.description: Same N03 fault as scenario 02, but 1s later the controller closes both tie lines (SW_N02_N05_TIE, SW_N04_N06_TIE) to restore N04, N05 and N06 through the alternate G01-N02-N05-N06-N04 path. Compare the restoration transient here against the permanently de-energized island in scenario 02.

scenario.name: Loop rejection
scenario.description: From the healthy baseline (no prior isolation), the controller asks to close the N02-N05 tie switch while N02-N03 and N03-N05 are still both closed. Closing it would form a closed loop (N02-N03-N05-N02), so PowerPlaneState.apply_command rejects the operation (accepted=false, reason 'rejected: closing line would create a closed-loop LV topology') as long as the pipeline is run with the default preserve_radial=True / without --allow-loops. The PSCAD switch state is left unchanged -- use this run to confirm the safety check holds and no loop current path is ever energized in PSCAD.

scenario.name: Degraded control-plane case
scenario.description: Same fault and restoration as scenario 03, but the reroute command is delayed by 40s (5s vs 45s) to stand in for a degraded/lossy AMRP LoRa uplink -- retransmission backoff or a missed gateway hop -- before the SDN controller's decision reaches the power plane. This scenario intentionally only changes the command timestamp gap (a property of this command-replay layer); it does not re-run seian_sim's own LoRa packet-loss model, since that simulator is kept unmodified per AI_CONTEXT.md. Use it to show how long N04/N05/N06 stay de-energized when the control channel itself is the bottleneck, versus the near-immediate restoration in scenario 03.

scenario.name: Physical fault with SDN restoration
scenario.description: A native PSCAD ABC-to-ground fault starts at N03 at 4.8 s. The controller isolates N03 at 5.0 s, the fault logic clears at 5.2 s, and the alternate N02-N05-N06-N04 path closes at 6.0 s.
